direction.name: The quiet instrument
direction.idea: Radical understatement. Where every competitor shouts, this page almost whispers: a headline barely larger than body text, a narrow column, small exact demonstrations, and a great deal of untouched space. The restraint is the claim. It says the thing is simple, finished and sure of itself. This only works when it is carried through completely; one loud element breaks it. In the study, a tool for simple lists sold itself with a 27px headline and 12–14px copy and was one of the most confident pages in the set.
direction.composition: A single column 440–560px wide, placed left of centre (starting at about 22% of the viewport width) or dead centre, running the whole page. The headline is the one large thing on the first screen: two lines at display size (5–7vw), medium weight, starting on the column's left edge and allowed to run wider than the column. The supporting paragraph follows at body size (17–19px) in the full ink. One small primary button and one text link. Below, each point is a short paragraph followed by a compact demonstration or image no wider than the column. Sections are separated only by space (96–140px). Nothing spans the full width until the footer, which is a single quiet line. The first screen is mostly empty and that emptiness is composed: the column's top edge sits at about 30% of the viewport height.
direction.typography: One family, two weights. A display size for the headline (5–7vw), one heading size for section titles (about 32–40px), body at 17–19px, a small size for captions (14–15px). Leading 1.5 for text. Letter-spacing near zero. The typeface must be handsome at small sizes.
direction.colour: Paper and two inks (full and soft). One accent used on exactly one element per screen.
direction.imagery: Precise rather than loud: cropped interface details at true size, and real photographs of the customer's world held to the column width, each doing one job. One short looping clip can sit at column width too. Never a large stock hero image.
direction.richness: Precision. With so little on the page, alignment, spacing and the exact size relationships are the design. Every element shares the column's left edge.
direction.pitfalls: This is the one direction where a small headline is right; the inspector will not object, but do not mix it with a large display line. Emptiness must look decided: keep the column edges exact and the vertical rhythm even. Not suitable when the subject needs emotion or photography to sell. Quiet is not thin: the column must still deliver every piece of content the brief asks for, in full, at 16px or more in the full ink. In blind tests the quiet version lost every time it was quiet everywhere: a small headline beside an empty panel read as unfinished. Quiet means few things, not small things: the headline and the demonstration are large, and every screen holds content.

hero.name: Object on the seam
hero.blueprint: A white or very pale page organised by one change of tone. A square-cornered panel one step darker than the page (a flat pale blue-grey or warm grey) fills the top 44% of the viewport inside 12px margins; the page colour runs below it. The object, photographed on a plain background and blended with `mix-blend-mode: multiply`, straddles the seam between the two tones: it is about 62% of the viewport wide, starts at column 6 and runs off the right edge, with its upper half over the panel and its lower half over the page. Type is small and exact. The headline is two lines at 24px in medium weight, far left on columns 1–3 at a 32px margin, its first baseline resting exactly on the seam; the second line is set in the softer ink. One supporting sentence at 15px, max 34ch, sits 120px lower on the same margin with the single action as a small rectangular button under it. A plain top row inside the panel at 14px: wordmark left, three text links centred, one text link right.
hero.mobile: The tonal panel takes the top 46svh. The object is 120vw wide, centred on the seam and cropped by the right edge. The headline sits just under the seam at 22px on two lines at a 20px margin, with the sentence at 15px beneath and then the button. The wordmark sits top-left inside the panel; the links collapse to one word top-right.
hero.headline: Two short sentences at 24px, one per line and up to about 28 characters each, the second in the softer ink.

type.note: A geometric grotesque with Scandinavian restraint: round letters, even colour, nothing decorative. Suits logistics, health, property and corporate sites that need to look clear and dependable.

palette.name: Graphite and orange
palette.note: Graphite and cool light-grey sections alternate, graphite taking about two thirds, and photographs are desaturated so nothing competes. Safety orange marks the buttons, one thick solid bar across the top of the page and the highlighted item in a list or chart.

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Narrow column, empty field
sections.blueprint: A single text column 300–340px wide, its left edge at 15% of the viewport width, starting 64px below the section top. It holds four or five short paragraphs at 15–16px with leading 1.5 and one blank line between them; the first paragraph is in medium weight and full ink, the rest in regular weight and the soft ink. No heading, no image, no button; one underlined text link may end the last paragraph. The remaining three-quarters of the 1440 screen is untouched ground, and the section is only as tall as the text plus 160px of padding below. The column's left edge must match a line used elsewhere on the page (the wordmark's left edge or a later column). Where the page has a large object or a fixed photograph, this column is the small text beside it. Holds 90–150 words comfortably.
sections.mobile: The column becomes 78% of the width, left-aligned at the 20px margin, so a strip of empty ground remains on the right as a deliberate margin. Text stays at 15–16px with the first paragraph in medium weight. Padding is 72px above and 96px below.

sections.name: Capabilities as a menu
sections.blueprint: The capabilities are set as a printed menu or price list. One paper-coloured sheet, 520–600px wide and taller than it is wide, sits on a contrasting flat ground, centred or starting at column 2; its top and bottom edges are cut into shallow scallops or a zigzag with clip-path, its sides straight. On it, centred at the top, the heading: two or three words at 44–56px, then 40px of space. Below, items in two or three groups; each group opens with its name at 20px bold. Each item is a row: the name at 19px on the left, a short value on the right (a price, a time, a quantity, 'included'), and between them a leader of round 4px dots (border-bottom: 4px dotted, sitting on the baseline). A description at 15px in the soft ink sits under the name, at most 34ch. 18px between items, 44px between groups.
sections.mobile: The sheet fills the width minus 12px margins and keeps its cut top and bottom edges. Names stay left and values right on one line with the dot leader between; descriptions wrap beneath at 15px. Group names drop to 18px. Padding inside the sheet is 20px.

sections.name: Frame run, one lifted
sections.blueprint: Columns 1–3 are a nearly empty column: the heading (two to four words at 24–28px) at the top, a link under it, and one or two short notes at 15px much further down, each level with the frame it describes. Columns 4–12 hold a run of six to eight frames of the same subject at one fixed height of 30vh, with natural widths and 6px gaps: the whole view, a tight crop of the same thing, a detail, the reverse side. The run is allowed to leave the right edge. One frame is lifted out of the row: shown at 2.2 times the row height with its bottom aligned to the row's bottom (flex row, align-items: end), so it stands above the others. Under each frame, at 15px: a name on the left and a single fact on the right. Square corners, no captions on the images.
sections.mobile: The heading and link sit on top. The lifted frame comes first at full width. The rest of the run scrolls sideways beneath it at a fixed height of 34vw with 4px gaps and scroll-snap, bleeding off the right edge. Notes are listed under the run at 15px.

references.name: Gil Huybrecht
references.idea: A portfolio as a contact sheet: every project is a numbered run of miniature page screenshots on black, and all text is set at one small size.
references.hero: Black field on a seven-column grid with 14px margins. The top band is plain white text at one size, about 16px: name in column one, availability in column two, a services list from column three, a longer awards list from column five, then 'Profile' and 'Email me' at the right. List items are indented one step under their label. Below the lists roughly 300px of black is left empty. At mid-height the thumbnail grid begins: one small website screenshot per column, about 190px wide, each topped by a number at its right corner, with the project name over the first of each run. Two tiny toggle chips sit in the bottom corners.
references.type: One neo-grotesk at a single size, about 16px (1.1vw), medium-bold with tight tracking, white on black, for everything: name, lists, labels, numbers, footer. There is no headline; hierarchy comes only from column position and indentation.
references.colour: #000000 #fcfcfc #272727 #8a8a8a — Pure black with white text; the only colour is whatever appears inside the screenshot thumbnails. Inactive toggle words drop to mid-grey on a dark grey chip.
references.imagery: Miniature full-page captures of the designer's client sites, uncropped at natural aspect ratios, square corners, no frames or shadows, about 190px wide, sitting directly on black.
references.layout: Seven equal columns with 14px gutters and margins for the whole page. Thumbnails align to columns but not to rows: each hangs from its own label at its own height, so bottoms are ragged. Projects flow continuously and wrap across rows.

sections.description: A seven-column field of screenshot thumbnails on black. Each project is a consecutive run of four to six thumbnails; the project name sits above the first, and every thumbnail carries its sequence number right-aligned above it in the same 16px white. Thumbnails keep their real proportions, so a row mixes 100px-tall and 280px-tall items with ragged bottoms and about 90px of black between rows. Runs break mid-row and continue on the next line with no divider.

View toggles. Two fixed chip pairs sit in the viewport's bottom corners: the left switches between a grid and a gallery view, the right between a normal and a novelty perspective mode. Each pair is a small dark-grey rounded rectangle containing two words, the active one white and the inactive grey, at the same 16px as all other text.

After about a screen of empty black, one band of text on the same seven columns: year and privacy link stacked at the left, then two columns of stacked social links, then two single links toward the right edge. Same size and weight as the header, no rule, no logo.

steal: Set every piece of text on the page at one size and weight and build hierarchy only from column position and a one-step indent under labels.
Show projects as numbered runs of uncropped page screenshots at natural heights on a strict column grid, leaving the bottoms ragged.
Leave a deliberate 300px void between the text header and the first row of work so the lists read as a letterhead.

references.name: Cursor Compile
references.idea: The event name drawn as seven looping one-line curves in seven colours, more signature than logotype, on an otherwise whisper-quiet off-white page whose images are re-rendered as rows of coloured characters.
references.hero: Warm off-white field with no header or navigation. Starting about 23% down, a line-drawn wordmark spans from 8% to 92% of the width and about 29% of the height: each letter is a single 2px stroke looping like a Lissajous figure, each in a different colour (orange, green, olive, lilac, black, brown, blue), overlapping its neighbours. Directly beneath, two 14px captions, one flush left in ink and one flush right in grey. After a gap of about 20% of the viewport, three equal columns sit at the bottom, each topped by a hairline: an 18px statement, a grey 14px paragraph, and an email field over a full-width near-black rectangular button.
references.type: The only large lettering is the drawn wordmark. All real text is CursorGothic regular in two sizes, 18px and 14px (the largest text on the page is 1.8vw), sentence case, with hierarchy made by ink versus mid-grey rather than by size or weight.
references.colour: #edece8 #26251e #f07a1f #2e9e3a #2f6bf0 #9b8ff0 — Warm paper ground with near-black and grey text. The wordmark's colours return one at a time as the single ink of each character-rendered image (lilac, teal, green, orange). Event photos are dark and warm.
references.imagery: Two kinds: landmarks and speaker portraits redrawn as rows of tiny characters in one saturated colour on a tint of the same colour; and dark, warm documentary event photos. All are square-cornered rectangles in strict rows.
references.layout: About 7% side margins on a three-column grid. Each section has a small two-line heading at left (title in ink, subtitle in grey), then a row or carousel of equal tiles with one-line captions beneath. Very large vertical gaps between sections; a denser photo grid near the end.

sections.description: Tour dates as a three-column grid of 3:2 tiles. Each tile is a city landmark rendered entirely in rows of small characters in one colour on a pale tint of that colour: lilac, teal, green, orange. Under each tile, one caption line: city name in ink, date in grey straight after it, and a status word flush right. A fourth tile wraps alone to the left of a second row, leaving two columns empty.

Session recordings as stacked carousels. A small heading and grey subtitle, then per stage a tiny label at left with two arrow glyphs at far right and a row of 16:9 dark photo tiles, two full tiles visible and a third cropped by the margin. Each tile has a small white event tag in its bottom-left corner. Caption beneath: speaker name in ink followed by the talk title in grey on the same line.

Speaker row: one-line heading at left, arrows at right, then four near-square portrait tiles with 8px gaps, each a face drawn in horizontal rows of characters in one colour on its tint (orange, green, lilac, teal). Some tiles show only plain stripes with the face barely emerging, so portraits appear to resolve from lines as they load or on hover.

After a three-column photo grid with mixed landscape and portrait crops and 8px gaps, the page ends on an empty off-white screen holding one centred sentence at 18px and a small dark pill button beneath it. There are no footer columns, links or legal rows.

steal: Draw the name as one continuous thin looping stroke per letter, each in a different colour, and let it be the only large element on the page.
Keep all text at two small sizes and build hierarchy from ink versus grey on the same line (name in ink, detail in grey right after it).
Re-render photographs as rows of tiny characters in a single saturated colour on a tint of that colour, one colour per tile.

references.name: Zara Webb
references.idea: A one-woman newborn-care practice presented like a hand-made keepsake: a mascot rabbit, scalloped and flower-shaped cut-outs, candid film photographs.
references.hero: Split exactly in half. Left, on cream: two-line mono caps nav stacks sit at the column's top-left and top-right with a handwritten script logo centred between them. Centred below, a five-line headline in a condensed serif, each line broken to one to three words so the block forms a ragged lozenge; then a three-line 16px sans paragraph and an outlined pill button in mono caps. A line-drawn rabbit on a skateboard rides a hairline at the column's bottom-right. Right: a candid flash photograph bleeds off the top and right edges and stops at 92% height; a lilac pill button and a round chat icon overlay its top-right corner.
references.type: Instrument Serif Regular for headings (52 to 57px, plus a 9.4vw footer wordmark), its italic for subheads and service names; Inter Tight for small body copy; PT Mono uppercase for nav, buttons and tiny captions; a script logo. Parenthesised italic numerals number the services.
references.colour: #fffdf1 #403630 #ece4d2 #e2c9f7 #cfe195 #f6e7e4 — Warm cream page with cocoa-brown text and two brown panels. Lilac marks the main pill button and footer wordmark; a sage-green pill marks a secondary action. Warm throughout.
references.imagery: Candid flash and film photos of babies and carers, some grainy black-and-white, cropped into non-rectangular masks (four-petal flower, scalloped egg) or small rounded portraits; plus black line doodles with halftone-dot fills: a recurring rabbit, flowers, a rattle, a bottle.
references.layout: 20px margins. Centred serif statements with small centred paragraphs alternate with split or inset blocks: a brown rounded panel, a half-photo half-beige block. Services run as a two-column hairline list. Doodles are tucked beside headlines; the footer's top edge is scalloped.

sections.description: A dark brown panel with about 11px radius, inset 20px from the page. Left half: a three-line cream serif statement at about 56px and below it a photograph masked into a four-lobed flower about 540px across, cropped by the panel's bottom, with two tiny mono captions floating beside its lobes. Right, from 63%: two blocks, each an italic serif subhead over a four-line small paragraph, then two flower doodles, a caps line and a lilac pill button.

A centred two-line serif heading and a four-line centred paragraph. Below, a two-column list inset to the middle 72% of the width; each item opens with a hairline, then a parenthesised italic numeral, the service name in italic serif at about 32px and a three-line small description. Rows are tall with generous empty space; the final cell swaps to a faded question prompt with the rabbit doodle.

A half-and-half block. Left: a grainy black-and-white extreme close-up of a baby's eye and cheek, full-bleed, overlapped from the bottom by a cream cut-out shaped like an egg with a scalloped top; it holds an italic serif subhead, a five-line centred paragraph, a caps line and a sage pill button. Right: a flat beige field with a centred two-line serif heading and a small rounded portrait about 230px wide flanked by two tiny mono captions.

Dark brown, its top edge cut into a row of twelve semicircular scallops about 120px wide. A centred three-line serif statement in cream with bottle and flower doodles at its shoulders and a waving rabbit beneath; two small centred text blocks at far left and right; contact lines and four social icons; then the name in lilac serif at 9.4vw, cropped by the bottom edge, with tiny mono legal text in both corners.

steal: Mask photographs into soft custom shapes (a four-petal flower, a scalloped egg) and let their container crop them.
Cut a section's top edge into a row of semicircles so a plain colour change becomes a motif.
Break a centred serif headline into very short lines so it forms a deliberate ragged shape, and anchor it with one small line drawing sitting on a hairline.
